questions.question: A phone field adds dashes from a `keydown` handler. What does `fill('5551234567')` leave in the field?
options: `555-123-4567`, because `fill()` sends each key
`5551234567`, because `fill()` sends no key events
An empty field, because masked inputs reject `fill()`
A timeout, because the field isn't editable
questions.explanation: `fill()` sets the text without key events, so the handler never runs. Use `pressSequentially()` when the page reacts to individual keys.

questions.question: An email rule runs when the field loses focus. After `email.fill('ada@')`, no error appears. What should the test do next?
options: Wait a fixed time with `page.waitForTimeout()`
Call `email.fill('ada@')` a second time
Dispatch a `keydown` event on the field
Call `email.blur()`, then assert the error
questions.explanation: `fill()` leaves focus in the field, so blur handlers haven't run. `blur()` or `press('Tab')` moves focus away as a user would.

questions.question: What happens when `selectOption(['US', 'UK'])` runs on a single-choice `<select>`?
options: Only the first match is selected, and no error is thrown
Both options are selected
It throws because the select isn't `multiple`
The last match is selected
questions.explanation: A single select takes the first match without complaint, so only an assertion such as `toHaveValue()` will reveal the mistake.

questions.question: An overlay covers a checkbox. What does `checkbox.click({ force: true })` do?
options: It removes the overlay and ticks the box
It ticks the box directly, ignoring the overlay
It reports success, but the click lands on the overlay
It always throws an actionability error
questions.explanation: Forcing skips the checks, but the click still happens at that screen position. The box stays unticked, and only an assertion will notice.

questions.question: A test sets `input.value` in `page.evaluate()` on a controlled React input and dispatches `input`. The field looks right, but the app's state is empty. What's the best fix?
options: Dispatch the `change` event twice
Use `locator.fill()` on the input
Add `{ force: true }` to the evaluate call
Wait for the network to go idle
questions.explanation: React tracks the value set by script, so it sees no change and doesn't call its handler. `fill()` enters text the way the browser expects and updates the state.
